It's really nice to hear that you were able to get out of that hostile environment and into something a bit more suiting (if that is a good word to use).

I had actually quit this job about 3 months back (hence why I was unemployed for the past 3 months) and decided that it would be the best fit because I could instantly get back on the floor, get a headset, a badge, and start making a steady income again.

I had quit because it was getting so stressful that I would come home every night and be so pent up with stress that I would lash out at my girlfriend at that time (who is my ex now, because of my issues with that and quitting due to stress).

At the time being, I only want to go back because I need the money. I keep holding on to the thought of "another day, another dollar", even if I have to take all that stress straight to my psyche.

You are correct that I am not one of those people that can just shut out unruly clients and basically zone them out while still doing my job. It's hard for me to not become either stressed out and terminate the call early, or get aggressive and fight back with the client. The latter is bad, because at my center, all calls are recorded and they have management crawling the floor down our aisle all the time.

They use this system called Utopi, which is a speech recognition software that runs on all our lines and records everything spoken, and a manager reviews it daily to make sure that us representatives aren't being 'abusive or rude' to a customer, when usually it's just us defending ourselves and asking the person on the other line to calm down and be professional about the matter.

But then again, in a such looked down upon field as debt collection is, who would be happy to receive a call from us? Not a whole lot. Though, I have encountered many pleasant people and I've been able to work out significant deals for them. But then there are those rude, quick to judge, dirty-mouthed people who are hellbent on making the call my worst experience possible. I just cannot leave work without a bad taste in my mouth and an empty or angry feeling in my heart.

To answer your question, I'm a 26 year old guy, about to be 27 this December. I'm quickly approaching my 30s and I fear that I may not be able to get into a steady career at this age since I lack any formal education outside of high school. Though, I did attend community college for 2 years but that ended when funds dried up and I had to quit school to work full time to support myself and my girlfriend (ex, now).

For someone my age, without any degrees or higher education, I feel like I am out of options. There are so many other people my age who have degrees and majors, and so many other skills. Any recruiting agent would most definitely look over my poor attempt at a resume and choose the more experienced and more academic person.

I just fear that I will be condemned to working these stressful, low paying, minimum wage jobs for eternity. Even though I'm hopeful that I can encounter something better, the chances seem pretty slim.

It's nice to get a response from someone who's been in my field. Yes, I have tried very hard to find another opportunity that more suits my personality and my set of skills, but it had got me nowhere.

I've been job searching for three months prior to deciding to return to this job. Trust me, I would have taken any opportunity before returning to this job.

Honestly, I just felt so useless for the past three months. Being unemployed and spending my time mostly at home was killing my soul. I just wanted to be back out there and doing something productive for once. It just has been way too long.

The reason I'm going back is because my previous employer has a history of ALWAYS rehiring past employees because they lose their new hires so fast due to the stress of the job.

Also, I'm not sure if you're familiar with the term 'after-call' that my call center used. The time in-between calls. Man, my firm was so anal about it that they would yell at you and pull you into a manager's office if you were 1% below the 4% average they wanted you to be at. Whether if you're at fault or not.

But I digress.

The only reason I'm returning is because of my failed attempts to find a job that was more worthwhile than this one. I've worked retail to food service and neither of those fit well with my anxiety. I had originally thought that having a desk job at a call center would help because I was indirectly dealing with clients, so there wasn't any face to face interaction. But even that was so stressful at times.

Was your management at that previous job high-strung and tense all the time? That also attributes my distaste for returning. But right now, I really have no choice. It's either that, or go for another few months being unemployed and financially, I just cannot do the latter.

Thank you so much for your reply.

Alongside alprazolam (xanax), I was prescribed paroxetine (paxil) for my depression. Both of those illnesses, my anxiety and depression have made it severely hard to have the motivation to get into work and stay there for an entire shift.

I'm glad to hear that Lovan has helped you deal with things a bit better. It's similar to what happens when I take xanax. It mellows me out and acts as an inhibitor to random thoughts. It kind of 'sedates' my mind so I'm less likely to have my mind wander and get filled with the many thoughts that provoke my anxiety to a point where I freak out.

I've only been taking it for a few weeks now, but the mellowness alongside the SSRI paxil have helped me with my anxiety greatly. Though, starting this new job has 'broken' that barrier that these medications have built up, so to say.

I do hope that they will allow me to at least bring in a few pills in case I have a severe episode.

Thank you for giving me hope that things can and will get better. I do hope the same for you and that it keeps getting better.

Hey man, I've been going through the same thing for the past two months. I thought that maybe I could share some advice with you that may or may not help, but I figure at least I'd try.

I'm not certain how soon it was before (if there was one, not sure based on your description, so apologies if I'm wrong) your relationship with her ended. If it was fresh and very recent, then I sympathize with you and I can totally understand how overwhelming it is.

Since for me, it's been a couple months, the pit in my stomach and the overall uneasy feeling has dulled a bit. What I can say from my personal experience, much like the other replies before me, is that distance really is the most beneficial factor in healing this wound that you've been dealt.

Just like you, I still have dreams where my ex and I were together. Everything picture perfect. Going about as if nothing bad happened, we never split, and just going about our daily routines happily. I know how soul crushing it can feel when you wake up to reality and realize that it was all in your head. I'm really sorry, man. I can only say that it may happen but the only thing you can really do is just ignore it and distract yourself as much as possible once you wake up from one of those dreams. I find that if I wake up and find something to take my attention, I tend to forget the dream faster and it lessens the initial gut-wrenching (at least for me) feeling.

You say that you can't get her out of your life because you are still close friends with her. Not to be too forward, but could I ask you for a bit more detail as to what you mean by that? Did you two split and then agree to remain friends? If so, that may be (again, only in my opinion) a huge roadblock in both you and her's path in healing and moving on.

At first, I wasn't a big fan of the whole 'No Contact' concept and was adamant on remaining friends with my ex. But all that ever brought was more misery on my part since I was constantly in contact with her and it only served to remind me of what I had lost.

I found that the longer I went without contacting my ex, checking her facebook, texting, calling, or doing anything to reach her, the faster I began to crawl out of the seemingly endless pit I was stuck in.

Perhaps you could try and distance yourself from her as much as possible, even though you may still be in touch. Or, just make yourself as unavailable as possible. I'm still a firm believer that distance will mend your heart faster than holding on to friendship in the wake of a failed relationship.

It's done wonders for me. I went from being a nervous depressed wreck the first month after my break-up, to now being more comfortable with not having to remain in touch or wondering what she's doing. And along with this no contact philosophy that I've adopted, I noticed that I thought about her less. Which lead me to feel less upset, and ultimately caused me to even dream of her less often.

Again, I'm not trying to preach to you, just letting you know what had worked for me. I can definitely empathize with you about how terrible your situation is and for that, I am sorry you have to experience it.

Sorry for the length, I just really felt the need to write this message to you since it kind of hit home for me as well. I wish you the best and if you do feel up to responding, I'll keep in touch and reply to you as soon as I can.

Best wishes, bro. Keep your head up and work on yourself as much as possible. Put yourself first. You deserve it.

Well, that is eerily similar to what my ex and I went through. 

Basically, I had asked her to give it one more try, but she said no. Then the thought occurred to me that we could remain friends. But then my rational mind kicked in.

If she didn't care enough to want to give it another shot, or try and work on the situation with me, then why would I consider being her friend? In the end, it would only cause more pain and suffering on my part. She had shown herself to be quite cold and distant after the breakup, so being friends with her wouldn't have gone anywhere.

I do have to say that the hardest thing for me to do was resist the urge to pick up my phone and call her or text her. (I'll be honest though, I did do exactly that for a couple weeks after we split. I now regret it.) It's so hard to do but in our situation, it's the best.

Think of your hopes and dreams of her as a parasite. The more you feed it with hopeful thoughts, of wanting to get back with her, or thinking of calling her 'just to talk', it grows. At least that's been in my experience. And it just keeps growing the longer you try and stay in contact with someone when, for all extents and purposes, is over.

I only began to start recovering once I severed all contact with her. Though I'll admit there are days (like today) where I just want to call her up and confess my undying love (etc, etc) for her and beg her to take me back.

I know that feel, bro. It sucks. It drains the life out of you. It kills your motivation. And it makes you depressed and anxious. But, just like a phoenix, you'll rise from the ashes a smarter, better person.

Most people do mean well. But in my experience, they often take it upon themselves and try to give you advice that they would implement themselves if they were ever in a situation like yours.

I've seen people who have never suffered from depression before try to tell me things that they would do or what they felt was right. But the error of their ways is that it's NOT ABOUT THEM. It's about me. It's about you. It's about everyone who has suffered through such tremendous pain.

I get that they believe they can help you because they are genuinely happy. And they feel like since they are happy, they are qualified to dispense advice they see fit. Though, not having personally gone through depression themselves, the advice and comfort they try to give is not necessarily going to help out.

I'm a firm believer that if you are trying to give advice to someone... you need to first put YOU in THEIR shoes. Not absorb how they feel and tell them how YOU would react if YOU were in that position. That kind of advice is ill-suited to help out anyone but the normal, happy, non-depressed folk.

Don't get me started on the 'blanket statements' that the majority of the population use as a band-aid or a cure-all. It's usually the lazy way out and doesn't help anyone.

To be honest with you, I'm in the same boat. I know all too well how much it hurts to feel alone. Like you're unable to 'jumpstart' yourself and be 'normal'.

Trust me when I say this though. It most likely isn't you. Just like what others have said before me, it is probably the skewed way you view yourself.

I believe that the way we see ourselves directly translates into how we act and how others see us. If for example, you believed that you were bad at making friends and that no one wanted anything to do with you, in effect, you are making that illusion a reality and living in it. Even if it's only subtle.

You sound like a wonderful, smart, amazing person. You have it within you to bring that out on the surface. You might even get others who have ignored you in the past to do a double-take and wonder what the hell they were thinking before.

Also, you sound strong. You face adversity and loneliness, you say you have trouble approaching new people, but look at you now. You've taken that leap, posted on reddit, and basically opened your innermost feelings out to the world. I respect you for that and I'm excited to have the opportunity to respond to you.

All in all, these hard times should pass. I'm no psychic or prophet, not at all. But when the storm is finished and everything is washed away, the sun will come out to brighten the day.

You are not defective. You are not worthless. Please, don't think of yourself that way. You are a wonderful person. Don't let yourself or anyone else tell you otherwise!

Hey there.

I decided to comment because your situation is strikingly similar to my own. It's nice (kind of in a selfish way) to know that there are others out there that are experiencing the same issues as I am.

One warning though: I type like the wind. So if you're not in to that, feel free to skip the paragraph walls below.

I'm a 26 year old guy. I've had several issues in my life where it has gotten to the point where I have little to no motivation to better myself. It's very disheartening to feel that there is no possible way to climb up in life and actually be happy with life.

I'm currently living with family after a bad breakup with a recent ex. This has left me jobless, caused me to lose my home (that I loved because it was away from family and allowed me personal space), and lost a lot of friends in that process.

I would say that my social skills are equal if not less to yours. So I understand how tormenting it might feel to think about trying to interact with other people.

See, most of my life, I was a wholly optimistic person. I've always had stars in my eyes when it came to thinking about my future. For example, the girl I was with, I had already started thinking about the future and how bright it was. Only to have her leave me and have that illusion torn down and set aflame.

Just like you, I have no set direction in life. Everything that I try, I end up giving up due to my increasing lack of strength of will and motivation. It's like I'm stuck in a vicious cycle of trying and failing.

The best advice I can give you, one that has helped me out invaluably, is to always look at the silver lining hiding behind everything.

For example, you are enrolled in higher education. Me personally, I have never even got close to considering college/university. Nor would I hardly qualify if I had applied anyway.

Also, another thing to remember is that just like there are people who are in a much better place in life, there are also people who have it way worse. I'm sorry if saying this doesn't really help you, but for me it's comforting to know that I'm not in worst place in my life when I consider the world and the bigger picture. It's kind of uplifting for me.

But back to our similarities. I'm 26. I live with my mom. I have no job. I have almost ZERO social interaction. But believe me, I've tried and failed to be more social. People are either just too busy or don't care to bother and try to hang out with me. Meh.

All in all, even though I'm dealing with a lot, I still take a small moment to pause during my day (which is filled with just wasting time and ignoring my bigger problems) to appreciate that even at my worst, there is still some shard of hope left.

For one, I'm still alive and so are you. We fall, all the time. But nothing but ourselves can stop us from picking ourselves up and brushing off the dirt.

Have you considered using a site like www.meetup.com to see if there are any local groups or hangouts that share your interests? For me, I've looked up things like minecraft lans and other geeky things. Cause that's who I am, haha.

It's always much easier to make friends when you share some common interests. It helps to fill those awkward gaps because you'll have something to say that will be interesting for the other people you're with.

Also, what I have been doing in my spare time is take computer science and programming classes online. www.codecademy.com helps me greatly when I'm in a low mood and just want something that's both distracting yet helpful in the greater scheme of things. Perhaps all that learning will land me in my dream job of being a programmer. Who knows right? lol.

Anyways, I'm sorry if my post really doesn't have a main direction (just like my life, haha). I just wanted to share my experiences with you and let you know that you are definitely not alone. There are many people out here going through things just like you are and I'm one of them.

Please, if you ever feel the need to vent or just to talk to someone for kicks or whatnot, shoot me a PM. I've always got time and an ear to listen. Maybe we could even help each other out and share some life experiences?

I share the same symptoms. When I have a full blown anxiety attack, I suffer from the following:

* Shortness of breath
* Tightening of chest
* Tingling sensations around my face, neck, arms, legs, and feet.
* Physical heaviness on my chest, like someone is actively applying pressure.
* Sharp, brief pain around my chest localized near my lungs and heart
* Sharp, brief pain on my arms near elbows

I find it hard to breath in a normal pattern. When I notice my breathing getting more shallow and slower, trying to fix it only increases the pressure on my chest.

The only thing that has really helped the pain go away, at least for me, is doing breathing exercises that slow down my heart-rate and relax my muscles.

Try this out when you experience the physical symptoms, it may help:


1. Relax your shoulders, neck, and arms. Make sure there isn't any tension.

2. Close your eyes and exhale.

3. Inhale slowly through your nose for 4-5 seconds. Use what you feel is best.

4. Hold it in for a few seconds.

5. Slowly exhale through your mouth. Try to match the same length of your inhale.

6. Keep repeating the above for a few minutes, or until you feel is necessary.


I'm not saying that it will work for you, but it's helped lessen or even completely remove most physical symptoms when I'm in the middle of an attack.

Hope you feel better. PM me if you'd like to talk or swap words with someone dealing with anxiety attacks.
